summary: Publish-PR CI reconciliation: MCP main keeps the library-owned hardcoded version literal (no var version), account.go registers novel commands via direct cmd.AddCommand, and comments sweep stops before any fetch estimated to exceed --max-credits (running-max per-fetch estimator; overshoot bounded by one fetch's actual-minus-estimated cost).
reason: Three library-side gates rejected the fresh 4.30.1 print shape. (1) The generator emits 'var version = ...' in cmd/<cli>-pp-mcp/main.go, but the public library's release-ledger workflow owns runtime version stamping; the base tree hardcodes the literal in server.NewMCPServer and the Verify guard blocks any change to it. (2) The generator attaches novel commands with addNovelCommandIfAbsent(...), which the library's verify_skill.py command-tree parser does not recognize (it matches only .AddCommand(newXxxCmd()), so account estimate/budget flags in SKILL.md/README hard-fail CI; direct cmd.AddCommand is what the previously published tree used. (3) Greptile P1: the sweep's pre-request budget check allowed overspending --max-credits by one fetch; the budget check now stops before any fetch whose estimated cost would exceed --max-credits, estimating with the maximum per-fetch charge observed in the run (floor 1, seeded from the initial posts fetch) on both comment fetches and posts-page fetches; per-request cost is server-side and only known post-response, so the residual overshoot is bounded by one fetch's actual-minus-estimated cost and credits_charged always reports the true total. All three must survive future reprints until fixed upstream in cli-printing-press.
validated_outcome: verify_skill.py all checks pass; version-declaration diff vs library main empty; go build/vet/test green on both trees.
